metadata.method: Keyword sweep across 2,839 UPSC Prelims PYQs with word-boundary matching. Subject filter: Medieval Indian History, Ancient Indian History, Art and Culture (352-question candidate pool). Node-label keywords + ~250 manual aliases (e.g., "Brihadeshwara"→"Rajarajeshvara", "Mahabalipuram"→"Mamallapuram rathas", "Rai Pithora"→"Prithviraja", "Dnyaneshwar"→"Jnaneshwar"). Era-spanning terms ("Kalinga", "Guilds", "Bhakti") treated with boundary tagging. Final triage pass rejected PYQs whose content is not answerable from era-4 nodes (era-2/3/5/6 + modern + current-affairs). Dropped PYQs preserved with reasons in metadata.dropped_in_triage for audit.

confidence_legend.high: Specific node-label match; clearly era-4 answerable from current node content
confidence_legend.medium: Era-4 content + partial overlap with era-3 (post-Gupta transition) or era-5 (Sultanate boundary)
confidence_legend.boundary: Answerable only partially from era-4 content (e.g., one of 4 pair-match options is in era 4)
confidence_legend.low: Era-4 content is adjacent/tangential; primary answer may require era-3/5/6 knowledge

metadata.note: Era-level question bank (NOT node-linked). UPSC questions frequently test multiple tied-together concepts, so node-associations are indicative, not exclusive. Boundary PYQs are valuable for cross-era comparative study.
